page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-88 is an x86_64 cloud instance configured with an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The machine delivers 88 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 44 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features a 105 MB shared L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8 instructions for matrix mathematics. System memory totals 704.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation that positions the platform firmly in the memory-dense tier.

The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage or physical GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage architectures. In benchmark suites, the server shows strong multi-threaded execution metrics, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 18538.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 73262.01. Single-core performance falls in the median tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks exhibit read throughput of 224.4 GB/sec and write speeds of 99.58 GB/sec, reflecting efficient bus interconnects across the large memory footprint.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, this server targets software stacks requiring massive memory capacity without incurring the expense of dedicated graphics processing units. Workloads that benefit most from this hardware profile include large in-memory databases like Redis, extensive Clang software compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, and large-scale data engineering or memory-constrained scientific computing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-88 is an x86_64 instance powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor, offering 88 vCPUs across 44 physical cores and 704.0 GB of memory. Designed with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPUs, utilizing external storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong multi-core scaling, reaching 74040.34 in PassMark CPU tests and 85.22 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, while single-core metrics remain within average ranges. Large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 224.4 GB/sec, underscoring substantial data transport capacity across RAM. This instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale in-memory caching tiers, big data analytics engines, enterprise database systems, and heavy multi-threaded software build pipelines.
